title: Prototypes and this
description:
Write three functions:

```javascript
function ownAndInherited(obj) { }   // { own: [...], inherited: [...] }: property names, each list sorted
function bindMethods(obj) { }       // binds every function-valued own property of obj to obj, in place; returns obj
function later(obj, methodName) { } // a function that calls obj[methodName] with its arguments and the right this
```

- `ownAndInherited` lists the enumerable own property names (`Object.keys`) and, separately, the enumerable names found on its prototype chain but not on the object itself (a `for...in` loop sees both). Each name appears once.
- After `bindMethods(obj)`, `const f = obj.method; f()` works with `this` as `obj`.
- `later(obj, "greet")` looks up the method **when it is called**, so replacing `obj.greet` afterwards changes what runs.
hints: `for (const key in obj)` visits enumerable names on the object and its prototypes; `Object.hasOwn(obj, key)` tells which ones belong to the object itself.
`obj[methodName](...args)` is a method call, so `this` is `obj`. Wrapping it in an arrow function delays the lookup until the call.
